TASK: The forklift operator was restacking fallen cartons from a damaged pallet in the shipping bay by hand. The task was underway because a pallet had shifted in transit and had to be restacked before the trailer could be loaded. Stage of the task: transport, moving or handling material. Method in effect: SW-140 Manual Restacking of Damaged Pallets. The task was not being performed as written. The difference from the written method was as follows: the written method calls for two people to restack a damaged pallet, but only one operator was in the bay at that hour and the trailer was due out. Equipment involved: A damaged wooden pallet and cartons in the shipping bay. Equipment state at the time: at rest or stopped. Equipment condition: The pallet had a broken top board which is why the load had shifted. Object handled weighed approximately 45 pounds per carton. Object size and shape: about 24 inches square with no hand holds. The object was held as follows: gripped underneath at opposite corners with both hands and held against the chest. PPE in use: Safety glasses, steel toe boots and general purpose gloves. This matched the PPE specified for the task.

SEQUENCE: Immediately before the event: squatting beside the damaged pallet with a carton at floor level, back turned toward the stack it was going onto. At the moment of the event: the carton was raised to about chest height and the torso twisted to the right to place it on the stack behind, at which point a sharp pain was felt across the lower back. Immediately after the event: the carton was placed on the stack, the operator straightened up slowly and continued restacking the remaining cartons more carefully, and the trailer was loaded on time.

MECHANISM: Load or force involved: approximately 45 pounds. The load moved from floor level to about chest height. Body position during the movement: the carton was raised at about 16 inches in front of the body with the back bent forward, then the torso twisted to the right without moving the feet. Assist device: A pallet jack and a lift table are available in the bay but neither helps with restacking cartons by hand, so nothing was used. This was a one-person lift. Point of contact and direction of force: across the lower back on the right side, with the load pulling forward and the torso rotating right.

CONDITIONS: Difference from a normal run of this task: The written method requires two people for a damaged pallet and only one operator was in the bay at that hour. Conditions at the point of injury: time or production pressure. Detail: The trailer was booked out within the hour and the bay was otherwise empty. Timing: About 10 hours into a 12 hour shift, the second consecutive day of overtime, and roughly 15 minutes into this task. The forklift operator had performed this task before. No known hazard, prior near miss, open action or risk assessment covers this task. No guard, interlock, barrier or control was bypassed, missing, defeated or ineffective. Stop-work opportunity: The restack could have waited for a second person, but that would have meant missing the trailer departure and no cover was available in the bay.

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS: First aid at the scene: No first aid was given at the time because the pain was not reported until the following morning. No first aid was given at the scene. Notification: The supervisor was told at the start of the following shift, about fourteen hours after the event. Reason for the delay in reporting: the pain was mild at the time and was expected to settle overnight, and the trailer still had to be loaded. It was worse the following morning. Scene and equipment: Nothing was secured because the event was not reported at the time. Work at the location continued unchanged. The forklift operator was sent to an offsite occupational clinic for evaluation.
